transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

For months now, I’ve had this constant heavy, sad feeling that I just can’t seem to shake, even when I’m doing things I used to enjoy. My primary care doctor noticed a big change in me during a routine check-up and recommended I get evaluated, which is why I'm here.

Have you had other separate periods in your life when you felt this depressed for weeks or months and then got back closer to your usual self in between? Or has your mood been low most of the time for at least two years without a break longer than about two months?
No, I’ve never really experienced periods of sadness like this before in my life. This low mood has only been present for the last eight months, so it hasn't been going on for two years.

During this depression, have you had any hallucinations, like hearing or seeing things others don’t, or very strong beliefs that others said were not true? This helps me understand how severe the depression is.
No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. I haven't seen or heard things that aren't there, and I don't have any beliefs that others have found unusual.

How much has this depression affected your daily functioning—are you still able to work, take care of yourself, and manage basic responsibilities, or has it become very difficult or impossible? Have there been times you couldn’t get out of bed or keep up with eating, bathing, or other basic self-care?

Since I'm retired, I don't have a job to worry about, and I can still manage basic self-care like bathing and eating. However, I feel so low and drained that I've let my art circle stall out and have started canceling plans with my friends. I'm also really struggling to keep up with my sister's medical appointments and paperwork, which used to be much easier for me to manage.

Have you ever had a period lasting several days or more when you felt unusually energetic or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked much more than usual, or acted impulsively? This helps rule out bipolar disorder as a cause of the depression.
No, I’ve never experienced anything like that at all. My struggle has really just been with feeling very low, heavy, and tired these past several months, never the opposite.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of harming yourself or wishing you were dead? If so, have you had any plan or intent to act on those thoughts?

On my really low days, I do sometimes think that if I just didn’t wake up one morning, it would be a relief for me and make things simpler for everyone. However, I absolutely do not have any plan or intention to actually hurt myself. It's just a feeling that comes over me when the weight of everything feels like too much.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a first depressive episode lasting 8 months with persistent sad/heavy mood, loss of interest in previously enjoyable activities, low energy, passive death wishes, and clear functional decline in social and caregiving responsibilities. There is no history of mania/hypomania, no psychotic symptoms, and the duration does not support dysthymia/persistent depressive disorder.
